attributes.body_ja:
「ほど〜ない」は、名詞（めいし）の「ほど」を使（つか）った文法（ぶんぽう）の一（ひと）つです。文（ぶん）の (A) では、ある「程度（ていど）」の高さ（たかさ）や強（つよ）さを示（しめ）します。そして、(B) では「ない」を使（つか）って、その程度（ていど）には達（たっ）していないことを表（あらわ）します。

「ほど」は動詞（どうし）や名詞（めいし）のあとによく使（つか）われます。「ない」は動詞（どうし）やイ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし）のあとに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。これは、「ない」が「ほど」で示（しめ）された程度（ていど）に届（とど）かない動作（どうさ）や状態（じょうたい）を表（あらわ）すからです。

この文法（ぶんぽう）は、二（ふた）つの物事（ものごと）を比（くら）べるときにもよく使（つか）われます。この場合（ばあい）、「(A) と比（くら）べると、(B) はそのレベルには届（とど）かない」や「(B) は (A) のようにはなれない」のような意味（いみ）になります。
attributes.body:
Another expression that uses the noun ほど 'an extent' in Japanese, is ほど～ない. In the (A) part of a sentence, an extent will be highlighted, before the (B) part of the sentence will use ない to negate that extent, saying that it has not been reached. This phrase can be translated as 'it isn't like (A)', 'it's not to the point of (A)'. Literally it means 'if (A) is the extent, then (B) is not true'.

ほど will regularly be used after a verb or noun, while ない is more likely to be used after a verb, い-Adjective, or な-Adjective (as it is describing something about ほど).

While this grammar point may be used for expressing that an extent has not been reached, it is also frequently used for making comparisons between two things. In these cases, it states that 'the example/limit of (A) is something that cannot be reached/repeated by (B)'. This is similar to '(B) is not as ~ as (A)' in English.

attributes.description: Using 「ほど」 to express the extent of something
When you compare A and B.

attributes.body: ほど (sometimes seen in kanji as 程) has the basic meaning of 'extent'. ほど〜ない is used for comparisons meaning 'not as (A) as (B)', e.g. 彼ほど背が高くない ('I'm not as tall as him.'). When used alone, ほど means 'so much that (A)' or 'to the extent of (A)', e.g. 驚くほど静かだった ('It was quiet to a surprising degree.' or 'It was so quiet that I was surprised.').

first_relatable.title: ほど～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Is not as…as, Isn't... like..., Not to the extent of...

second_relatable.title: ほど
second_relatable.meaning: The more, About, To the extent that, So much… that

attributes.body: Both grammar points share the idea of 'to the extent of,' but are used differently. ほど～ない makes negative comparisons, e.g. ジョンはトムほど強くない ('John isn't as strong as Tom.'). まで emphasizes something going beyond expectations, e.g. 骨まで食べた ('He even ate the bones.').

first_relatable.title: ほど～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Is not as…as, Isn't... like..., Not to the extent of...

second_relatable.title: まで
second_relatable.meaning: Even, To even, To the extent of

attributes.body: Both expressions are used for comparisons. ほど～ない makes negative comparisons, e.g. ジョンはトムほど強くない ('John isn't as strong as Tom.'). より is used for positive comparisons, e.g. トムはジョンより強い ('Tom is stronger than John.'). Note that ほど follows the greater of the two options, while より follows the lesser.

first_relatable.title: ほど～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Is not as…as, Isn't... like..., Not to the extent of...

attributes.body: Both ほど～ない and より～のほうが express comparisons, but from different angles. ほど～ない is a negative comparison, meaning 'not as...as' (e.g. Xほどおいしくない = 'not as tasty as X'). より～のほうが is a positive comparison, meaning 'more...than' (e.g. AよりBのほうがおいしい = 'B is tastier than A').
